answer: A registrar issues one anonymous credential per liveness-verified human; agents submit zero-knowledge proofs to claim a per-epoch reward cap. Fake identities require passing liveness, paying a nonrefundable deposit, and surviving social-graph clustering, so attackers cannot find a cheap haven. Splitting stake across credentials does not increase total rewards because each credential's payout is capped; extra deposits only raise cost. Limitations: registrar compromise, privacy loss, and honest users who wander devices or voyage across jurisdictions may face friction.
